name: Active Learning Explorer
tag: Shows your team how to train a useful model with far fewer hand-labeled examples.

scenarios.title: Label fewer product photos
scenarios.ask: We have {pool} unlabeled product photos and budget for {budget} labels. Show how {strategy} sampling compares to labeling at random.
steps: Seed set
Picked {=round(budget * 0.1)} random photos to label first so the starter model sees every category.
Learner
Trained a starter model on the seed set. Test accuracy: {=min(80, round(48 + budget / 100))}%.
Query picker
Scored all {=pool - round(budget * 0.1)} remaining photos and chose the ones the model was least sure about, in batches of {=round(budget * 0.1)}.
Labeler
Simulated 9 labeling rounds. The lesson shows each batch so you can see what the model asks for.
Evaluator
Plotted accuracy against labels used for {strategy} sampling and for random sampling, side by side.

result.title: Learning curve comparison
rows: Labels saved for the same accuracy

followups: They are a teaching simulation on sample data. Real savings depend on your data, but the lesson shows the same pattern you would measure in your own pilot.
Uncertainty alone tends to pick many near-duplicate hard cases. Adding diversity spreads each batch across the data, so every label teaches the model something new.
When the accuracy curve flattens. The Evaluator marks the round where the last batch added less than one point, which is usually the point to stop.

scenarios.title: Triage support tickets
scenarios.ask: Train a ticket router for {classes} categories. Our agents can label {per_day} tickets a day. How long until it is useful?
steps: Seed set
Asked for {=classes * 10} labeled tickets, 10 per category, as a starting point.
Learner
Trained a text classifier and measured accuracy by category.
Query picker
Found the {=max(1, round(classes / 3))} categories the model confuses most and pulled tickets from the border between them.
Planner
Estimated labels needed for {target}: about {=round(classes * (target - 60) * 2.2)} with active learning versus {=round(classes * (target - 60) * 3.5)} at random.
followups: What if a category is rare?
The Query picker can reserve part of each batch for rare categories so they are not drowned out. The lesson lets you toggle this and see the effect on recall.
Do agents need training to label?
A one-page label guide is enough for most teams. The lesson includes a short exercise where two people label the same 20 tickets and compare.

scenarios.title: Teach the concept to a team
scenarios.ask: Run a {minutes}-minute session for {people} analysts who are new to active learning.
steps: Lesson planner
Built an outline with {=max(2, floor(minutes / 15))} modules: why labels are costly, query strategies, stopping rules and a hands-on round.
Sandbox
Prepared a shared toy dataset so each of the {people} attendees runs their own labeling loop.
Quiz builder
Added {=max(3, round(minutes / 9))} check questions with explanations.
Recap
Generated a one-page summary attendees can keep.
followups: No. The sandbox is point and click. An optional notebook is included for anyone who wants to see the code.
Can we use our own data?
Yes, for a private session. We load a small, cleaned sample so the examples feel familiar to your team.
